newsitem.title: USA: Guidant Q2 beats estimate, sales growth stunted.
newsitem.headline: Guidant Q2 beats estimate, sales growth stunted.

text.p: Guidant Corp on Wednesday reported second-quarter earnings of $0.63 per share, beating the Wall Street consensus estimate by a penny and topping year-ago earnings of $0.53 per share.

The medical devices manufacturer said second-quarter sales rose six percent to $281 million over a year ago, but trailed an 18-percent quarterly gain in sales volumes due to currency, pricing and product mix effects.

Total revenues for the medical devices manufacturer were reduced three percent by unfavorable currency movements and by nine percent due to "worldwide product mix changes and international price erosion."
Shares in Guidant were up 11/16 to 87-5/8 at midday.
"Both our implantable defibrillator and pacing businesses are doing exceptionally well," said chief executive Ronald Dollens in a statement accompanying quarterly results.
Both the current and year-ago second-quarter earnings figures excluded special charges related to acquired in-process research and development and other issues.

On a segment basis, cardiac rhythm management sales grew to $164.4 milllion, up 14 percent over a year ago. Sales of the company's Ventak implantable defibrillators drove growth, while pacemaker sales also set an all-time record for sales performance worldwide, the company said.

Second-quarter sales in the vascular intervention group fell seven percent to $101.1 million from a year ago. The company said it has submitted a premarket approval application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for its ACS Multi-Link coronary stent, which analysts said they expect to be a major product for Guidant.
Second-quarter sales of in the minimally invasive systems group were $15.5 million, up 27 percent over the second quarter of 1996, Guidant said.
Research and development expenditures for the quarter were $42.4 million, up from $37 million a year ago.
"The quarter's 15 percent growth in research and development expenditures reflects the company's continued commitment to funding of future new technology and product initiatives," Guidant said.
Adjusted gross profit margin for the first half of the year rose to about 74.7 percent from 71.4 percent a year ago.
"Continued increases in manufacturing efficiencies and favorable foreign currency hedging results in 1997 led to an 11 percent increase in gross margins over adjusted 1996 results," the company said.
